rationale: Round 8. Round 7 was REVISE with guardian's veto RESOLVED (it approved) and 10 of 12 seats approving; two medium objections remained and both are answered here by CHECKING, not arguing. (1) bug_historian — a genuine catch and now FIXED IN CODE: parseReportedConditions flagged 'the whole field is broken' but a MIXED list silently dropped its junk entries while the survivors made the response look wholly healthy — the same silence one level down. It now returns a skipped count; persistReportedConditions warns 'partly UNPARSEABLE — some entries were dropped and are lost; the surviving ones are not the whole picture, fix the emitter'. New test TestParseReportedConditionsMixedListReportsWhatItDropped pins exactly the case asked for (3 valid + 2 junk → 3 parsed, skipped=2, NOT flagged wholly malformed), and the existing junk test now asserts skipped=3. Committed 8ec9e2ab8. (2) prior_art_librarian's DORMANT-MACHINERY challenge — was diagnosis_artifacts already the home for this? CHECKED against the live DB, and the answer is no: it holds only fix-loop artifacts (fix_plan 111, council_report 78+44, bundle 59, escalation 5), written solely by diagnose-agent and fix-loop actions (diagnose_persist_fix_plan_action.go, diagnose_assemble_bundle_action.go, fixloop_digest_action.go); NO adapter writes it. Structurally it also cannot serve this need: of {severity, resolved, work_item_id, site_id} it has only site_id, so there is no resolved=false unresolved-condition query and no equivalent of idx_error_log_unresolved — the dashboards and immune-system sweep read agent_error_log precisely because that is where severity+resolved live. Its correlation_id keying is per-diagnosis-run, not per-response. (3) The same seat asked me to confirm buildErrorEntry/logAgentError pre-exist unchanged rather than being introduced by this round: git log -S proves both date to c24aa7411, 2026-03-12 ('built simple error logging to db'), four months before this change; this plan adds callers, not implementations. MATERIAL DISCLOSURE, unprompted: the round-6 form of this code is ALREADY LIVE IN PRODUCTION. Another session's sweep commit (bca5d8255, v1.0.1140, 17:11Z) swept my then-uncommitted working tree into its build, and both services rolled at ~17:58Z. Verified against the running binaries, both replicas of both services, greping strings this change CREATES: chassis 'UNSANCTIONED sender'=1, 'Persisted adapter-reported conditions'=1, 'the reporting contract broke'=1 (positive control 'site provider preference applied'=1); adapter 'UNROUTED_IMAGE_KIND'=1, 'REFERENCE_ANCHORS_DROPPED'=1 on both replicas (positive control 'UNROUTED KIND'=1). This was not my doing and I am not treating it as approval: no Council-Reviewed trailer has been or will be claimed on a non-approved verdict, and the round-7/8 fix above is inert until the next roll. It does mean the gate reviews code that is already serving traffic, which reviewers should weigh — the contained-alternative gate is what makes that tolerable: every non-sanctioned pipeline is provably unaffected. Substance otherwise unchanged from round 6/7: guardian's contained alternative (a) implemented verbatim — persistence GATED on response.Headers.Sender.AgentType against conditionReportingAgentTypes = {image-generator}; unsanctioned senders warned by name and never persisted; alternative (b) (output_contract) rejected for putting a config lookup in the fleet's hottest path and for the documented re-seed clobber landmine making the gate's ground truth mutable outside code review, with senderMayReportConditions as the single swap seam. The adapter stays DB-free; the chassis never re-derives the routing table; the coupling is one field name plus one consumer-owned allowlist. Underlying problem unchanged: routing guards die in pod logs — proven today when a hero's routing decision's only witness was a log line on one of two replicas.

plan.summary: The image adapter's routing guards (UNROUTED KIND, bad provider_hint, dropped reference anchors) currently die in pod logs. Add a pure reportedConditions() next to the routing table that turns routingDecision flags into condition records; thread them through generateImage into the success response body as `reported_conditions`; on the chassis, parseReportedConditions + persistReportedConditions in agent_error_log.go write each to agent_error_log (severity 'warning', resolved=false, sender identity from response headers), called once from handleCompleteResponse — reachable only after ProcessResponse's atomic claim (no duplicate persists), and now GATED on an explicit sender allowlist (guardian's round-5 contained alternative) so every non-sanctioned pipeline is provably untouched. Absent field = healthy case (one map lookup); present-but-malformed = loud contract-break warning, never a silent healthy-looking nil (bug_historian's round-5 catch); old chassis ignores the field, old adapter sends none, so the two images may roll separately.

plan.risks: 1) Hot path: for every non-sanctioned pipeline the call is now provably one map lookup (gate short-circuits before parse); for sanctioned senders, parse + best-effort inserts only when conditions exist. 2) The allowlist is a hand-maintained list IN THE CONSUMER — deliberate: it is an authorisation record, mismatches fail LOUD (named warning), and it does not predict another binary's config, so it is not the routing-table drift class; if architecture review later prefers declaring via output_contract, senderMayReportConditions is the single swap seam. 3) No dedup across responses: N unrouted generations = N rows (capped 10/response; per-response duplicates impossible via the atomic claim). Row count is the signal's size; rows group by error_code. 4) Contract-break behaviour: a MIXED list now warns with an explicit dropped/parsed count rather than losing entries behind healthy survivors (round 8); malformed field → conditions LOST for that response (warned, not persisted) — the alternative, persisting a synthetic 'malformed' row, was rejected as inventing data; the warn names the emitter to fix. 5) Split-roll safe both directions: old chassis ignores the field; old adapter sends none. 6) Best-effort semantics inherited from logAgentError.
